This is the list item parsing. `beg` is the prefix of the list item (e.g., `- `). Then `is_codefence(data + beg, end - beg, ...)` is called on the content after the list marker. So if we have a list item like `- ` followed by 3 spaces, then `data + beg` points to the 3 spaces and `end - beg` would be 3.

Wait, but `end` is computed as: `end = beg; while (end < size && data[end - 1] != '\n') end++;`. So `end` goes to the end of the line. If the line is `-    ` (dash, space, then 3 spaces), then beg=2 (after `- `), and end would be 6 (end of line). So `end - beg = 4`, not 3.
